title: On Windows, ending the shared Codex app-server does not end its descendant tree: vendor housekeeping (git plugin sync) outlives the root by seconds
outcome: When TermAl ends a shared Codex app-server (clear_shared_codex_runtime_if_matches), every descendant process the app-server started ends with it, or the product records it as an unowned survivor. Today SharedCodexRuntime owns only a SharedChild for the root and has no process-tree owner. In the first real vendor proof for w-24055bbb2390, the root PID 92328 was gone at the after-cleanup snapshot, but five git processes it had started for its own plugin catalogue sync (git fetch https://github.com/openai/plugins.git, plus remote-https and index-pack) were still running, with cwd in the disposable CODEX_HOME and in the host directory. They exited on their own about 3 s later. They held no cwd in the delegating worktree, so w-24055bbb2390's criteria do not cover them. This is the Windows counterpart of w-aac85dbd4c4c, which covers Unix descendant cleanup.
acceptance: On Windows, ending the shared Codex app-server does not end its descendant tree: vendor housekeeping (git plugin sync) outlives the root by seconds is done
